record.original_question: Let Γ be the subcomplex of Δ(σ, π) induced by those permutations τ in the interval [σ, π] with μ(σ, τ) not equal to 0. Determine whether Γ must always be pure, meaning that all of its maximal simplices have the same dimension.

evidence.quote: 2. Let Γ be the subcomplex of ∆(σ, π) induced by those elements τ of [σ, π] for which µ(σ, τ) 6= 0. Is Γ a pure complex, that is, do all its maximal simplices (with respect to inclusion) have the same dimension?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S = \bigcup_{n\ge 1} S_n$ be the set of all finite permutations, where $S_n$ is the symmetric group on $\{1,\dots,n\}$ written in one-line notation. Define the pattern containment order on $S$ by declaring $\sigma \le \pi$ if there exist indices $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \le n$ (with $\sigma \in S_k$, $\pi \in S_n$) such that the subword $\pi(i_1)\pi(i_2)\cdots\pi(i_k)$ is order-isomorphic to $\sigma$. Under this order $S$ is a graded poset (rank given by length).

Fix $\sigma < \pi$ in $S$ and consider the open interval $(\sigma,\pi) = \{\tau \in S : \sigma < \tau < \pi\}$. Let $\Delta(\sigma,\pi)$ denote the order complex of $(\sigma,\pi)$: the abstract simplicial complex whose vertices are the elements of $(\sigma,\pi)$ and whose simplices are the chains $\tau_0 < \tau_1 < \cdots < \tau_r$ in $(\sigma,\pi)$. Let $\mu$ denote the Möbius function of the closed interval $[\sigma,\pi]$, defined recursively by $\mu(\sigma,\sigma)=1$ and $\mu(\sigma,\tau) = -\sum_{\sigma\le\rho<\tau}\mu(\sigma,\rho)$ for $\tau>\sigma$.

Let $\Gamma$ be the subcomplex of $\Delta(\sigma,\pi)$ induced by the vertex set $\{\tau \in (\sigma,\pi) : \mu(\sigma,\tau) \neq 0\}$; that is, $\Gamma$ consists of all chains in $(\sigma,\pi)$ whose elements all have nonzero Möbius value $\mu(\sigma,\cdot)$.

Question: Must $\Gamma$ always be pure, i.e., must all maximal simplices of $\Gamma$ (with respect to inclusion) have the same dimension, for every choice of $\sigma < \pi$ in $S$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered negatively by McNamara and Steingrímsson in their work "On the topology of the permutation pattern poset" (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A, 2015; arXiv:1305.5569). They exhibit a counterexample, with the interval $[213, 254613]$ identified as a counterexample of minimal top-element length, showing that $\Gamma$ need not be pure in general.

status_evidence.title: On the topology of the permutation pattern poset (McNamara–Steingrímsson)
status_evidence.snippet: First explicit major results on the topology of intervals in the permutation pattern poset, addressing among others the purity question of the nonzero-Möbius subcomplex.
status_evidence.claim: The paper resolves the purity question, providing a counterexample [213, 254613] of minimal top-element length showing Γ need not be pure.

status_evidence.title: On the topology of the permutation pattern poset – Strathprints PDF
status_evidence.snippet: Published in J. Combin. Theory Ser. A, March 2015.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexample to the purity of the subcomplex induced by τ with μ(σ,τ)≠0 is given.
